brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut to market-fair band (₹0.65–0.80/pc on caps) and tighten payment to 15 days, freeing ₹2.39 L cash, while qualifying Manjushree Technopack as a robust second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% reduction on rigid plastic packaging, targeting the lower end of the market-fair range.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.65–0.80/pc for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps (vs typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc)
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking prices for 28 mm PP caps sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The market verdict is MARKET-FAIR with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec. We spend ₹58.17 L annually — enough volume to justify the lower band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days after receipt to 15 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹2.39 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Suraj Blow Plast publishes no financials, so we can't assess their health or cash position directly. Our ₹58.17 L annual spend gives us weight, but without their numbers we must rely on outside options to create pressure. We have five strong alternates lined up — including Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, B health score) and three listed players. That lineup lets us push firmly on price and payment without needing to guess their finances.

evidence.point: We spend ₹58.17 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging — a material volume that should command better terms.
The open-market typical ask for 28 mm PP caps is ₹0.85–0.95/pc, with headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at scale.
HDPE resin import unit value stands at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material cost anchor.
Tightening payment from 30 days to 15 days frees up ₹2.39 L of our cash.

Manjushree Technopack — the country's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — is a proven pharma supplier with ₹2569.83 Cr revenue and a B (65/100) health score, making them a credible second source.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, specializing in pharma bottles, caps and preforms; ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, B health score — the top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader serving pharma with pails, containers and closures — strong, profitable and a robust alternate for bottles and caps.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed player in moulded and blow-moulded packaging with broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Suraj Blow Plast does not publish financials, so we fly blind on their cash position and stability — watch for any signs of delivery slip or quality fade.
Pushing too hard on both price and payment at once may spook a smaller private supplier; consider phasing the asks or offering a volume commitment in return.

We have no internal price benchmark (no bestPriceWePay) for rigid packaging, so our ask rests entirely on the external market line — confirm the ₹0.65–0.80 band with a quick RFQ to one alternate before the meeting.
The market-backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are unqualified web findings — do not treat them as approved sources until we verify capability and run an audit.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but at ₹58.17 L a year we need pricing that reflects the market — caps are trading at ₹0.65–0.80 at volume, and we'd like to close that gap while moving to 15-day payment to free up working cash for both sides.
